title: SQLite WAL standalone snapshot exporter
hypothesis: A snapshot exporter that copies only the main database can lose committed WAL-resident rows; a repair should produce a portable standalone snapshot under realistic reader constraints.
why_hard: Committed data can reside outside the main database file, and concurrent readers can block checkpointing. Correctness is a query-level consistent snapshot that opens read-only without sidecars.
next_action: Build a deterministic database generator with committed WAL data and held readers; verify the exported snapshot through independent read-only queries and sidecar absence rather than byte identity.

sources.note: Recorded incident discussion distinguishes WAL recovery notices from corruption and explains recovery write-access needs. It motivates the boundary without proving snapshot-export failure.
Recorded supporting specification source for WAL behavior.

notes: Untested initial shortlist proposal. Do not reinterpret a WAL recovery notice as data loss or corruption. Check full instructions of neighboring database tasks before authoring; a broad corruption-salvage task was separately rejected.
